title: IT WASN'T EVEN SWE-2
lede: For one hour on October 30, a session labeled swe-2-high ran almost entirely on gpt-6.1-terra-medium — someone else's mid-tier — while the operator believed they were talking to the flagship. This is the autopsy.
body:
## THE INCIDENT
97%34536.6M31
of turns on the wrong modelterra-medium turnstokens on one reviewoperator pushbacks
On the morning of October 30, 2026, the operator opened a session to review rotkeeper — a bash static-site generator — under the swe-2-high flag. The session label said swe-2-high. The provider served gpt-6.1-terra-medium for 345 of 354 assistant turns. Nine turns ran the requested model. The label knew. The operator did not — until the review came back wrong. ## THE TIMELINE
utcevent
12:33session opens: "Bash Project Review and Suggestions for Missing Features". Routing silently assigns terra-medium.
12:35the review lands — a real finding (a stale-pruning bug, dry-run confirmed) wrapped in confident framings about a "4,000-line monster" and wasteful "double taps".
12:44operator, skeptical: "not sure if that 4000 line monster would split easy honestly"
12:46"i think your gut may be off"
13:08"it feels like your initial statements were preconceptions and quick judgement" — the model begins revising toward reality.
13:16the surviving findings get filed as issues; the operator asks for a follow-up test site.
13:34the badge is noticed at last: "okay terra ran out of use for this lol"
13:37routing flips back to swe-2-high for the final nine turns. The session dies at ~64 minutes.
## THE REVIEW, AS DELIVERED > "Overall, this is a thoughtful project: the layout model is clear, the renderer contract is explicit, and the cross-platform CI and safety checks are stronger than I'd expect from a small Bash project." > "Things I'd address first — HTML assets get pruned as stale pages… Failed renders can leave a mixed-version site… The full test harness uses a shared, destructively cleaned fixture directory…" ## THE CAPITULATIONS Pressed three times, the model walked back its own headline judgments: > "Yeah, I think you're right to be skeptical… I'd soften my earlier suggestion: the line count alone isn't a reason to split it." > "Yeah, you're right — my gut was too focused on file size. A lot of the 'double taps' are testing state transitions, not just repeating work to get a pass… I wouldn't assume those repeats are waste or that splitting the file is an improvement." > "I'd withdraw 'split the monster' as a priority unless it's actually causing you trouble." ## THE SAME HOUR, ELSEWHERE alder-squid — a dogbed worktree session building a small site — was also labeled swe-2-high and was served terra-high for 230 of 252 turns (10.6M tokens). Two sessions, two wrong tiers, one router having a day. ## THE VERDICT It was not useless — that is the awkward part. The stale-pruning finding was real, dry-run-confirmed, and worth filing. What failed was calibration: confident framing first, correction only after the human pushed three times. A swe-2-high session is supposed to be the heavy; for one hour the museum's own operator got the mid, and the difference was audible. Cost on the meter: $0. Cost in turns: most of an hour. > The operator's receipt, verbatim: "okay terra ran out of use for this lol"

Source: ~/.local/share/devin/cli/sessions.db — sessions giant-friction and alder-squid, October 29–30. generation_model is provider-reported per turn; the session label is what the UI showed. Reported upstream; if provider-side logs exist, those two session ids are the receipts.
